title: Dylan Harper Reveals the Hilarious Thing Spurs Players Have Been Teaching Victor Wembanyama - NewsBreak
text:
By Kenny Nosay ,
1 hours ago
Dylan Harper and Victor Wembanyama (Photo by Imagn Images) Victor Wembanyama may have looked like a veteran at times during this year’s playoff run by the San Antonio Spurs. He has spoken like one , too. However, while his grasp of American English has been developing, some of his teammates have told him how to swear more.
There’s no doubt that whenever a non-American gets drafted or signed by an NBA team, most of them struggle with communication. They might be able to understand what their American coaches and teammates say, but it usually takes 2 or more years before they become fluent. And Wemby is no exception.
Even his rookie teammate, Dylan Harper, has said that he and some of his Spurs teammates have taught the 7-foot-4 French star how to properly use curse words.
“We taught him [Victor Wembanyama] bad words. I feel like it’s been the other way around,” per Dylan Harper.
In return, Harper and some Spurs players may have also learned how to curse in French. They could all use that, though. For example, Lakers star Luka Doncic is known to curse in his native Slovenian, often directed at either the refs or other players.
The point is getting your frustrations out, but without triggering a possible technical.
Victor Wembanyama’s Rise Already Being Compared to the Greats In just his third year, Wembanyama has led the San Antonio Spurs to the NBA Finals. This is his first postseason experience. And he’s only 22 years old. With that in mind, basketball analyst Brian Windhorst has already compared Victor Wembanyama to another legendary player who excelled at that age and had a similar experience.
And who is that player? It’s none other than LeBron James . For additional context, James led the Cleveland Cavaliers to a 2007 NBA Finals berth at just 22 years old. However, LeBron and the Cavs were brutally swept by the Tim Duncan-led Spurs in the Finals back then.
Can Wemby win it all in just his third year? His team definitely has the right mix to do it.
